newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea union says will hold strikes once a week.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea union says will hold strikes once a week.

text.p: South Korean union workers will return to work on Monday and limit their industrial action to once a week, a top strike leader said on Saturday.
But he warned that the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions would stage an "all-out struggle" from February 18 if the government did not scrap a controversial new labour law.
"From next week, full strikes will take place only on Wednesday. On other week days, union members will work normally," confederation president Kwon Young-kil told a news conference.
"On every Saturday, we will hold protest rallies after work," he added.
The move follows intense government pressure to halt more than three weeks of strikes in protest at the labour law, which allows companies to dismiss workers and replace strikers.
The government has called the strikes illegal and prosecutors have warrants to arrest Kwon and six deputies holed up at Seoul's Myongdong cathedral.
